unit.title: Advanced connectors & discourse markers
unit.subtitle: no obstante, por consiguiente, dado que, a pesar de que, es decir

grammar.title: The linkers that make writing sound educated
grammar.intro: Basic connectors (pero, porque, entonces) work, but formal and written Spanish reaches for richer links. Learn a set for contrast, consequence, cause, concession, reformulation and summary, and your essays and emails will sound like a native professional's.

sections.heading: Contrast and consequence
sections.body: For a formal “however”, use no obstante or sin embargo. For “therefore”, use por (lo) tanto, por consiguiente or así pues:

ex.es: Es caro. No obstante, vale la pena.
ex.en: It's expensive. However, it's worth it.

ex.es: No hay pruebas; por consiguiente, se cierra el caso.
ex.en: There is no evidence; therefore, the case is closed.

sections.heading: Cause: “given that / since”
sections.body: To give a reason formally, use dado que, puesto que, ya que or debido a que + a clause. They often open the sentence:

ex.es: Dado que llueve, nos quedamos en casa.
ex.en: Given that it's raining, we're staying home.
We didn't go, since it was late.

sections.heading: Concession: “despite / although”
sections.body: Use a pesar de que + a full clause. With just a noun or an infinitive, drop the que: a pesar de + noun/infinitive:

ex.en: Even though he studied, he failed.
Despite the cold, we went out.

sections.heading: Reformulation, summary and addition
sections.body: To rephrase, use es decir or o sea (that is). To wrap up, use en definitiva or en resumen. To add, use además or the formal asimismo:

ex.es: Es bilingüe, es decir, habla dos lenguas.
ex.en: She's bilingual, that is, she speaks two languages.
In short, the proposal is worthwhile.

takeaways: Contrast: no obstante / sin embargo (however). Consequence: por (lo) tanto / por consiguiente / así pues (therefore).
Cause: dado que / puesto que / ya que / debido a que + clause (given that / since).
Concession: a pesar de + noun/infinitive; a pesar de QUE + a full clause.
Reformulation: es decir / o sea. Summary: en definitiva / en resumen. Addition: además / asimismo.

mistakes.w: A pesar de que el frío, salimos.
mistakes.why: With a noun (el frío) drop the 'que': a pesar de + noun. Keep 'que' only before a full clause.

mistakes.w: A pesar de estudió mucho, suspendió.
mistakes.r: A pesar de que estudió mucho, suspendió.
mistakes.why: Before a conjugated clause you need 'a pesar de QUE'.

mistakes.w: Por consiguiente que no hay pruebas, se cierra el caso.
mistakes.r: Dado que no hay pruebas, se cierra el caso.
mistakes.why: Por consiguiente marks consequence, not cause; use dado que / puesto que for the reason.

exercises.prompt: Es caro. ___, creo que vale la pena.
exercises.prompt_en: It's expensive. However, I think it's worth it.

exercises.prompt: No hay pruebas; ___, se cierra el caso.
exercises.prompt_en: There is no evidence; therefore, the case is closed.
exercises.no: To mark a consequence (“therefore”), use “por consiguiente”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “Given that it's raining, we're staying home.”
exercises.no: “Dado que llueve, nos quedamos en casa” — dado que introduces the cause.

exercises.prompt: A pesar de ___ estudió mucho, suspendió el examen.
exercises.prompt_en: Even though he studied a lot, he failed the exam.
exercises.hint: Before a full clause (estudió), you need this word.
exercises.ok: ¡Bien! Ante una oración → a pesar de que.
exercises.no: Before a conjugated clause use “a pesar de que”: a pesar de que estudió.

exercises.prompt: Match each connector to its function.

exercises.tts: A pesar del frío, salimos a caminar.
accepted: a pesar del frio salimos a caminar
a pesar del frío, salimos a caminar
exercises.translation: Despite the cold, we went out for a walk.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “A pesar del frío, salimos a caminar.”
exercises.no: It was: “A pesar del frío, salimos a caminar.” (Despite the cold, we went out for a walk.)

options.text: En definitiva, el proyecto es viable y conviene aprobarlo.
Dado que el proyecto es viable y conviene aprobarlo.
Es decir el proyecto es viable y conviene aprobarlo.

exercises.no: To sum up a conclusion, open with “En definitiva” (in short).

exercises.say: No obstante, vale la pena intentarlo
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “No obstante, vale la pena intentarlo”.

vocab.en: even though / despite the fact that
